content.user_title: Build Firestore Enterprise Native Mode Apps
content.value_statement: Firestore Enterprise Native Mode setup requires careful provisioning, rules, indexes, and SDK choices. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code focused guidance for secure Firebase implementation.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to create a Firestore Enterprise database with Native mode settings.
Outlines firebase.json, firestore.rules, and firestore.indexes.json setup steps.
Guides secure Firestore Security Rules generation with validation and ownership checks.
Shows Web SDK and Python SDK patterns for reads, writes, transactions, and queries.
Describes dense, sparse, composite, and unique index configuration for Firestore Enterprise.
Provides a security review checklist for rule bypass, privilege, and data exposure risks.
limitations: It does not provision cloud resources unless the assistant runs Firebase CLI commands separately.
It cannot verify project-specific IAM, billing, or Firebase console state by itself.
Generated security rules still need application testing and human review before launch.
Examples use placeholder database IDs, collection names, and app data structures.

use_cases.title: Provision an Enterprise Database
use_cases.description: Create the local Firebase files and CLI plan needed for a Firestore Enterprise Native Mode database.

use_cases.title: Harden Firestore Rules
use_cases.description: Generate owner checks, schema validation, immutable fields, and attack tests for sensitive application data.

use_cases.title: Plan Queries and Indexes
use_cases.description: Map SDK query patterns to required Firestore Enterprise index definitions and deployment steps.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up My Database
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new Firebase project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me set up Firestore Enterprise Native Mode for my Firebase project. List the files I need and the commands I should review.

prompt_templates.title: Create Secure Rules
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate rules generation from an app model.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate prototype Firestore Security Rules for these collections, fields, auth roles, and queries. Include validation and ownership checks.

prompt_templates.title: Review Rule Weaknesses
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Firestore rules for bypasses, PII leaks, role escalation, missing update validation, and unsafe public reads.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize Query Indexes
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced index planning for production queries.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these Firestore queries and propose the required dense, sparse, composite, or unique indexes for Enterprise Native Mode.

output_examples.input: I need a locked-down starting point for a new Firestore Enterprise app.
output_examples.output: A setup plan with Firebase files, a default-deny rules approach, deployment commands to review, and validation next steps.

output_examples.input: My users collection stores email and display names. Can profiles be public?
output_examples.output: A security recommendation to separate private user data from public profile data and restrict private reads to the owner.

output_examples.input: These queries filter by status and sort by created time.
output_examples.output: An index plan that identifies required fields, ordering direction, query scope, and deployment considerations.

best_practices: Start with default-deny rules and add the minimum required access for each collection.
Validate create and update operations with the same schema and ownership requirements.
Test generated rules against abuse cases before sharing production data widely.
anti_patterns: Do not make a users collection publicly readable when it contains private fields.
Do not rely on ownership checks without validating all updated fields.
Do not deploy indexes or rules without reviewing the affected Firebase project.

faq.question: Does this skill create Firebase resources automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and command examples. The assistant must run commands separately with appropriate user approval.

faq.question: Can it generate production-ready Security Rules?
faq.answer: It can generate strong prototypes. You should test and review them against your real app before production use.

faq.question: Does it support both Web and Python SDK usage?
faq.answer: Yes. The references include common read, write, transaction, query, and pipeline examples for both environments.

faq.question: Can it help with Firestore Enterprise indexes?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains dense, sparse, composite, and unique indexes with configuration guidance.

faq.question: Does it replace official Firebase documentation?
faq.answer: No. It organizes common implementation guidance, but official Firebase documentation remains the source of truth.

faq.question: Is it useful for existing Firebase apps?
faq.answer: Yes. It can review existing queries, rules, and index plans for Firestore Enterprise Native Mode migration work.
